raw_response:
I will do it mostly the way I did before, because 5 mu is not big, and if I miss the harvest, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on fertilizer. I farm wheat and maize on the same land, one after the other, so I will treat the 5 mu as wheat first, then maize after wheat comes off. I have a well, so I am not as scared of dry weather as people without water, and I will use that water when the crop really needs it. For wheat, I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I have seen people around me get steadier grain that way. I will put a heavier fertilizer base before or at sowing, then topdress once when the wheat starts growing strong in spring. I will still use some phosphorus for roots and some potassium so the stalk is stronger. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because around here people plant hybrid maize and it usually fills better than old seed. I will put manure or base fertilizer if I have it, then chemical fertilizer in two times, one at planting and one when the maize gets knee-high to waist-high. I would rather feed maize a little more than leave it hungry. I will not do fancy things. I will follow what works on fields around me, keep the land turned and leveled, water in time, spray when I see real pest or disease pressure, and try to keep costs under control because fertilizer, seed, spray, and water all come from the same pocket.
